items.question: How do I book or reschedule an appointment?
items.answer: Patients can use the dashboard to view upcoming appointments and contact the appropriate department for changes. If you need a same-day change, call the front desk listed for your clinic.

items.question: What should I bring to an in-person visit?
items.answer: Bring a photo ID, your insurance card, a current medication list, and any recent test documents you want the care team to review.

items.question: Why can I see my details but not edit everything permanently?
items.answer: This course project supports in-browser updates for demonstration. Permanent profile changes would normally require a connected backend and secure account storage.

items.question: How do I recover access if I forget my password?
items.answer: Use the account recovery option on the sign-in screen or contact the patient support desk for identity verification and a password reset.

items.question: Can doctors manage prescriptions from their dashboard?
items.answer: Yes. The doctor dashboard includes a prescription queue so providers can review refill requests and medication actions for their assigned patients.

items.question: Why are some doctor schedule items marked with different statuses?
items.answer: Statuses help providers prioritize work. For example, Checked In means the patient is ready, while Next Up or Later Today helps sequence the remaining shift.

items.question: What can an admin do on the management page?
items.answer: Admins can create user accounts, update roles, suspend or reactivate users, and approve access-related requests from hospital staff.

items.question: Do role changes save permanently?
items.answer: In this project, role and status updates are handled in the browser for demonstration. In a production system, those actions would persist through a secure database and audit trail.

items.question: Where can I ask about insurance or billing issues?
items.answer: Use the billing support channel listed below. Have your patient ID, visit date, and insurance information ready so the team can help faster.

items.question: Which medications require provider approval?
items.answer: Prescription medications and controlled substances require provider authorization. Over-the-counter items may remain visible without approval requirements.

items.question: How long do refill requests usually take?
items.answer: Routine refill requests are typically reviewed within one business day, while controlled or specialty medications may require additional confirmation from the care team.
